items.summary: Keep ContextLattice native memory plugin and provider discovery in the Rust agent runtime.
items.rationale: This is an intentional Rust-native enhancement that improves memory orchestration and does not replace or remove upstream behavior.

items.summary: Preserve webhook-driven sync queue worker architecture with sqlite, SQS, and Kafka support.
items.rationale: Queue backend plurality (sqlite/SQS/Kafka) is an ultra reliability extension for upstream sync maintenance and does not reduce upstream parity scope.

items.summary: Preserve launchd-based interactive dev lifecycle management for webhook listener and worker.
items.rationale: launchd lifecycle is a macOS operational hardening layer for development upkeep and is intentionally additive.

items.summary: Track the upstream skills and optional-skills catalogues imported into this tree, the upstream skill paths kept elsewhere here or replaced in Rust, and the upstream skills not yet imported.
items.rationale: At upstream reference f64e4f4f5768, skills/ and optional-skills/ hold 917 local and 951 upstream files: 755 byte-identical (66 of them Python), 39 modified locally, 123 local only and 157 upstream files missing locally. The Rust runtime treats the catalogue as content: `hermes skills sync` copies skills/ into the user's skills directory, optional-skills/ is installed on request, and no Rust skill loader runs skill scripts. Python files in skills run only when the agent's terminal or code tools run them on the user's machine, or as a declared bootstrap command after approval when a skill is installed from a hub. Of the 157 missing files, 98 are present under another path: 96 files of 9 skills and the gaming category description, which upstream keeps under optional-skills/, are bundled here under skills/ (godmode under red-teaming/ rather than security/, obliteratus under mlops/inference/), so sync installs them by default; and the hermes-agent references native-mcp.md and webhooks.md correspond to the standalone native-mcp and webhook-subscriptions skills here. 2 are replaced for reasons recorded in queue-overrides.json: petdex by the Rust /pet catalogue (6fd839ac84d0) and the Cloudflare parse_deploy_output.py script by `hermes cloudflare parse-temporary-deploy-output` (ff08e60c63ad). 57 are absent with no recorded reason: optional-skills/security/unbroker (56 files) and skills/computer-use/SKILL.md (this tree has only the older skills/apple/macos-computer-use). They are the gap to close in the staged upstream refresh. The path prefixes name only these upstream paths, so other upstream skill drift fails the surface coverage gate.

items.summary: Keep platform adapter parity in the Rust gateway instead of vendoring upstream Python platform-plugin trees.
items.rationale: Platform behavior is represented by Rust-native gateway adapters, delivery helpers, auth/config readers, and adapter contracts; upstream Python plugin files are reference-only and must not become runtime execution paths in the Rust-first repo.

items.summary: Own Chronos managed-cron behavior in the Rust cron scheduler and API server instead of vendoring the upstream Python cron plugin.
items.rationale: Hermes Ultra implements NAS-mediated Chronos provisioning, callback JWT verification, stale/duplicate fire suppression, background dispatch, and post-fire re-arm in hermes-cron plus the Rust API server. The upstream plugins/cron_providers Python files are reference-only and must not become Rust runtime execution paths.

items.summary: Track the upstream Raft Python platform plugin as non-runtime until a Rust-native Raft adapter is scoped.
items.rationale: No Rust gateway Raft adapter is registered locally. Ultra preserves Rust-only runtime behavior and does not vendor the upstream Python wake-bridge adapter; this remains an explicit platform-gap item rather than an unclassified missing plugin tree.

items.summary: Track upstream Python backend plugin trees that are not yet closed as Rust-native runtime surfaces.
items.rationale: dashboard_auth/nous, dashboard_auth/drain, and security-guidance remain upstream-only Python plugin trees after this review. Hermes Ultra keeps runtime behavior Rust-native; these paths stay tracked for dedicated parity slices instead of being silently vendored.

items.summary: Do not import upstream implementation-plan archive documents unless they change local runtime or release behavior.
items.rationale: The upstream s6-overlay plan is a post-implementation reference document for upstream Docker/Python service-management history; Hermes Ultra tracks relevant runtime parity through local Docker, gateway, and release gates.

items.summary: Upstream Vertex Python provider plugin files stay reference-only; the Vertex provider is ported to Rust in hermes-agent::vertex.
items.rationale: The Rust port of agent/vertex_adapter.py and the vertex plugin lives in crates/hermes-agent/src/vertex.rs (VertexProvider, token cache, base URL from project and region, 401 re-mint) and crates/hermes-agent/src/vertex/credentials.rs (service-account RS256 JWT bearer grant, authorised-user refresh-token grant, Compute Engine metadata server, in google-auth's ADC order). It is selected by provider id vertex and its aliases in hermes-provider-runtime and the agent loop's runtime routing, listed in the CLI provider catalogue and setup wizard, and reads VERTEX_CREDENTIALS_PATH, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, VERTEX_PROJECT_ID, VERTEX_REGION and the vertex: config section. ADC external_account, impersonated and GDCH credential types, metadata-server mTLS and the Vertex thinking_config extra_body hook are not ported. The Python plugin files are reference-only and are not vendored into the Rust runtime.

items.summary: Treat Rust CLI/TUI and gateway as primary UX surface; upstream web/ui-tui trees are tracked as intentional divergence unless explicitly ported.
items.rationale: User-facing runtime parity is provided via Rust CLI/TUI/gateway. Web/ui-tui trees remain tracked and auditable, but not auto-vendored.

items.summary: Keep Honcho and Mem0 memory provider behavior in Rust-native memory/provider surfaces instead of vendoring Python plugin trees.
items.rationale: Honcho and Mem0 are tracked as rust-native memory_plugin entries in the adapter feature matrix and covered by Rust memory/config contracts; upstream Python plugin files are reference-only.

items.summary: Keep OpenRouter and Krea image generation provider behavior in the Rust image backend instead of vendoring upstream Python plugin trees.
items.rationale: crates/hermes-tools/src/backends/image_gen.rs implements OpenRouter-compatible image output, Nous-compatible routing, and Krea direct/managed transports with Rust tests; upstream Python image plugin files are reference-only.

items.summary: Upstream's DeepInfra, Fireworks AI and Upstage Solar Python provider plugins stay reference-only; the 3 providers are ported to Rust provider profiles.
items.rationale: crates/hermes-agent/src/provider_profiles.rs carries each provider's base URL, aliases, API key variable and reasoning_effort contract (DeepInfra clamps to the model's levels, Fireworks passes the effort as written, Upstage defaults to medium), with setup entries, model fallbacks, live catalogues and auxiliary models in hermes-cli and hermes-agent. Fireworks attribution headers are not ported. The Python plugin files are reference-only.

items.summary: Upstream's DeepInfra image and video generation plugins are not ported.
items.rationale: The Rust image and video tools have no DeepInfra backend; DeepInfra is available here for chat only. Port when a user needs DeepInfra media models.

items.summary: Upstream's model-written memory retrieval query is not ported.
items.rationale: Upstream's plugins/memory/query_rewrite.py has an auxiliary model rewrite the latest user message into a memory search query. The Rust memory providers search with the message as written. Port with the auxiliary.memory_query_rewrite setting.

items.summary: Upstream's per-source profile routing for one gateway is not ported, so its design note is not carried.
items.rationale: docs/profile-routing.md documents gateway/profile_routing.py, which picks a profile per platform, server, channel or thread. The Rust gateway serves one profile per run; run one gateway per profile instead.

items.summary: Nous Portal billing and the Hermes desktop app are upstream products this port does not ship.
items.rationale: docs/billing-lifecycle.md maps the TUI's /subscription and /topup states to Nous's billing service, and skills/hermes-desktop-plugins teaches plugins for the Hermes desktop app. This port takes no payments and has no desktop app, so the slash commands are allowlisted in slash-command-divergence.json and these files stay upstream's.

items.summary: Upstream moved these skills after July 2026; this tree keeps each at its earlier path.
items.rationale: Between b51fbc73 and v0.23.2 upstream moved these skills between skills/ and optional-skills/ or between categories. Each is present here under its earlier path, which upstream no longer has: optional-skills/autonomous-ai-agents/opencode is skills/autonomous-ai-agents/opencode here; optional-skills/creative/ascii-art is skills/creative/ascii-art here; optional-skills/creative/heartmula is skills/media/heartmula here; optional-skills/creative/pretext is skills/creative/pretext here; optional-skills/creative/sketch is skills/creative/sketch here; optional-skills/devops/inference-sh-cli is optional-skills/devops/cli here; optional-skills/media/gif-search is skills/media/gif-search here; optional-skills/media/songsee is skills/media/songsee here; optional-skills/mlops/evaluation/evaluating-llms-harness is skills/mlops/evaluation/lm-evaluation-harness here; optional-skills/mlops/models/segment-anything-model is skills/mlops/models/segment-anything here; optional-skills/research/blogwatcher is skills/research/blogwatcher here; optional-skills/research/llm-wiki is skills/research/llm-wiki here; optional-skills/research/research-paper-writing is skills/research/research-paper-writing here; optional-skills/smart-home/openhue is skills/smart-home/openhue here; optional-skills/software-development/hermes-agent-skill-authoring is skills/software-development/hermes-agent-skill-authoring here; optional-skills/software-development/node-inspect-debugger is skills/software-development/node-inspect-debugger here; optional-skills/software-development/python-debugpy is skills/software-development/python-debugpy here; skills/software-development/codebase-inspection is skills/github/codebase-inspection here; skills/software-development/dogfood is skills/dogfood here; optional-skills/creative/comfyui is skills/creative/comfyui here; optional-skills/creative/excalidraw is skills/creative/excalidraw here; optional-skills/finance/polymarket is skills/research/polymarket here; optional-skills/mlops/inference/llama-cpp is skills/mlops/inference/llama-cpp here; optional-skills/mlops/inference/serving-llms-vllm is skills/mlops/inference/vllm here; optional-skills/creative/design-md is skills/creative/design-md here. Moving a skill between skills/ and optional-skills/ changes whether it is installed by default, so the paths stay; the category files upstream moved with them, optional-skills/mlops/{evaluation,inference,models}/DESCRIPTION.md, are byte for byte this tree's skills/mlops/{evaluation,inference,models}/DESCRIPTION.md. The content is not merged: in 22 of the 25 skills this tree's copy differs from upstream's in 44 files, and upstream has 1 file(s) this copy lacks (optional-skills/research/research-paper-writing/references/phase5-paper-drafting.md). No gate compares moved files; these are merged one skill at a time.

items.summary: New upstream skills that carry scripts are not imported yet.
items.rationale: These skills are new upstream since b51fbc73 and ship Python, shell or JavaScript programs. This tree requires skill scripts to start programs by trusted path, never from the working folder (tests/skills/test_skill_program_lookup.py); each script is checked against that rule before its skill is imported. Code-free new skills were imported at the v0.23.2 re-pin. 3 of them are upstream merges of skills this tree ships (upstream c49fa88b): skills/software-development/github from the 5 skills/github skills, skills/productivity/pdf from nano-pdf and ocr-and-documents, and skills/productivity/microsoft-office from powerpoint.

items.summary: Files upstream added to skills this tree already carries are not merged.
items.rationale: Upstream added references, templates or scripts to these skills after b51fbc73. This tree's copy of each skill predates them and its SKILL.md does not name them, so adding the files alone would leave them unreferenced; the skills are merged one at a time. skills/AGENTS.md is upstream's authoring guide and names Python modules this tree does not have.

items.summary: Upstream Python plugins and plugin files added after July 2026 are not ported.
items.rationale: Upstream added these Python plugin trees and files between b51fbc73 and v0.23.2: remote configuration backends, chat platforms without a Rust adapter here (A2A, Buzz, Google Chat, Photon, Teams), model providers (Actual, Command Code, Meta AI, Nebius Token Factory, Router, Solstice), web search backends (Keenable, OpenAI native, Perplexity), Meta AI image and OpenRouter video generation, and the shared plugin loader, storage and helper modules. Discord, Signal, QQ Bot, Weixin, BlueBubbles, WhatsApp Cloud, Gemini, LM Studio, Tencent TokenHub and DDGS have Rust implementations here (crates/hermes-gateway/src/platforms, crates/hermes-agent, crates/hermes-tools/src/backends/web.rs); the files upstream added to those plugins are not ported or compared with the Rust code yet. Computer use (cua-driver, crates/hermes-tools/src/backends/computer_use.rs) and subagent delegation (delegate_task) also have Rust implementations; upstream's new plugin wrappers for them (plugins/computer_use, plugins/delegation/default) are not compared. The dashboard session-token auth provider has no Rust counterpart.

items.summary: Skills this tree ships that upstream retired, merged or moved after July 2026.
items.rationale: Upstream had these 35 skills at b51fbc73 and no longer has them at the same path at v0.23.2: it retired some and merged others into new skills (for example c49fa88b merged the skills/github skills into skills/software-development/github and nano-pdf, ocr-and-documents and powerpoint into the pdf and microsoft-office skills). This tree still ships them. Whether each should follow upstream is not decided; no gate checks files only this tree has.
